feature: Anti-vacuity rule in evaluator.md Mode 1 (Phase 1 vacuous feature detection)
problem: The evaluator currently has no instruction to detect 'vacuous feature' contracts — feature-typed tasks where all ACs test only file existence, content, or JSON structure with no runtime behavioral assertion. feat-role-model-config passed negotiation despite every AC being a grep/file-exists check. The spike-vacuous-feature-detection research recommended a prompt-only Phase 1 rule as the lowest-cost, highest-value first step.
proposed_solution: Add an anti-vacuity check to the 'What to challenge' section of evaluator.md Mode 1 (Contract Negotiation). The rule: if the contract task_id starts with feat-, verify at least one AC tests a runtime behavioral change, not just file existence/content. Commands like grep -c, test -f, python3 -c open(), and make [target] && test -f are file-interrogation only. If every AC is file-interrogation, REJECT and ask the builder to either add a behavioral AC or retype as chore. Include worked example and explicit exempt types.
acceptance_criteria:
evaluator.md Mode 1 'What to challenge' section contains the anti-vacuity rule — verified by section-scoped grep: python3 -c "import re; t=open('library/cursor/agents/evaluator.md').read(); m=re.search(r'^### What to challenge[^
]*
(.*?)(?=
### |
## |\Z)', t, re.S|re.M); assert m, 'section not found'; sec=m.group(1).lower(); assert any(p in sec for p in ['vacuit','vacuous']); assert any(p in sec for p in ['feat-','prefixed feat','task_id']); print('PASS-AC1')"

The rule names ALL four file-interrogation pattern categories (grep, test -f, python3 -c open(), and make+test -f file side-effects) — not merely 2 of 5: python3 -c "import re; t=open('library/cursor/agents/evaluator.md').read(); m=re.search(r'^### What to challenge[^
]*
(.*?)(?=
### |
## |\Z)', t, re.S|re.M); assert m; sec=m.group(1).lower(); assert 'grep' in sec, 'missing grep'; assert 'test -f' in sec, 'missing test -f'; assert 'python3 -c' in sec and 'open(' in sec, 'missing python3 -c open() pattern'; assert 'make ' in sec and ('side-effect' in sec or 'side effect' in sec or 'file side' in sec), 'missing make+side-effect callout'; print('PASS-AC2')"

The rule positively defines behavioral AC (not just what is NOT behavioral) — must state that a behavioral AC tests that the system works differently before vs after the change: python3 -c "import re; t=open('library/cursor/agents/evaluator.md').read(); m=re.search(r'^### What to challenge[^
]*
(.*?)(?=
### |
## |\Z)', t, re.S|re.M); assert m; sec=m.group(1).lower(); assert any(p in sec for p in ['works differently','behavioral change','runtime behavioral','before and after','application behavior']), 'missing positive behavioral definition'; print('PASS-AC3')"

The rule includes an explicit REJECT instruction (not merely push back or warn) when all ACs are file-interrogation, plus remediation (add behavioral AC or retype as chore): python3 -c "import re; t=open('library/cursor/agents/evaluator.md').read(); m=re.search(r'^### What to challenge[^
]*
(.*?)(?=
### |
## |\Z)', t, re.S|re.M); assert m; sec=m.group(1).lower(); assert 'reject' in sec, 'must say REJECT not just push back'; assert 'chore' in sec and ('retype' in sec or 're-type' in sec or 're type' in sec), 'missing retype-as-chore remediation'; print('PASS-AC4')"

The rule explicitly lists chore, spike, and docs as exempt task types NOT subject to the vacuity check: python3 -c "import re; t=open('library/cursor/agents/evaluator.md').read(); m=re.search(r'^### What to challenge[^
]*
(.*?)(?=
### |
## |\Z)', t, re.S|re.M); assert m; sec=m.group(1).lower(); assert 'chore' in sec and 'spike' in sec and 'docs' in sec; assert any(p in sec for p in ['exempt','does not apply','not subject','only applies']), 'missing explicit exemption language'; print('PASS-AC5')"

make sync-local propagates the updated evaluator.md to .cursor/agents/evaluator.md and the anti-vacuity rule is present in the synced copy's What to challenge section: make sync-local && python3 -c "import re; t=open('.cursor/agents/evaluator.md').read(); m=re.search(r'^### What to challenge[^
]*
(.*?)(?=
### |
## |\Z)', t, re.S|re.M); assert m, 'section not found in synced copy'; sec=m.group(1).lower(); assert any(p in sec for p in ['vacuit','vacuous']); print('PASS-AC6')"
edge_cases:
EC1: The anti-vacuity rule must be scoped to feat- prefix only — rule text must explicitly state feat- contracts are in scope and chore/spike/docs are exempt (no fragile OR keyword soup): python3 -c "import re; t=open('library/cursor/agents/evaluator.md').read(); m=re.search(r'^### What to challenge[^
]*
(.*?)(?=
### |
## |\Z)', t, re.S|re.M); sec=m.group(1).lower(); assert re.search(r'(task_id|contract).{0,40}feat-', sec) or re.search(r'prefixed.{0,20}feat-', sec) or re.search(r'feat-.{0,30}(only|contracts?)', sec), 'feat- scoping not explicit'; assert re.search(r'(chore|spike|docs).{0,60}(exempt|does not apply|not subject)', sec) or re.search(r'exempt.{0,40}(chore|spike|docs)', sec), 'exemption phrasing not explicit'; print('PASS-EC1')"

EC2: The rule must not bloat the evaluator.md file beyond its existing structure — total line count must stay under 300: python3 -c "lines=open('library/cursor/agents/evaluator.md').readlines(); assert len(lines)<300, f'Too long: {len(lines)} lines'; print(f'PASS-EC2 ({len(lines)} lines)')"

EC3: The worked example must cover the feat-role-model-config pattern exactly — make sync-local combined with test -f, explicitly labeled as file side-effect not behavioral change: python3 -c "import re; t=open('library/cursor/agents/evaluator.md').read(); m=re.search(r'^### What to challenge[^
]*
(.*?)(?=
### |
## |\Z)', t, re.S|re.M); sec=m.group(1).lower(); assert 'sync-local' in sec, 'missing sync-local in worked example'; assert 'test -f' in sec; assert 'make ' in sec; assert any(p in sec for p in ['side-effect','side effect','file side','not behavioral']), 'example must label make+test -f as non-behavioral'; print('PASS-EC3')"

round_1.AC1: ACCEPTED — section-scoped regex already targets ### What to challenge; tightened keyword list to require vacuity term + feat- scoping
round_1.AC2: STRENGTHENED — was '2 of 5 patterns' which allowed omitting make+side-effect; now requires all four categories including explicit make side-effect callout
round_1.AC3: STRENGTHENED (new) — split from old AC1/AC2; requires positive behavioral definition ('works differently before vs after'), not just negative file-interrogation examples
round_1.AC4: STRENGTHENED — was AC3; requires REJECT specifically (not push back) plus retype-as-chore remediation
round_1.AC5: STRENGTHENED — was AC4; added docs to exempt list per spike recommendation; requires explicit exemption phrasing
round_1.AC6: STRENGTHENED — was AC5; sync-local check now section-scopes the synced .cursor copy, not whole-file keyword match
round_1.EC1: STRENGTHENED — replaced fragile OR keyword soup with proximity regex requiring feat- scoping AND chore/spike/docs exemption in same sentence neighborhood
round_1.EC2: ACCEPTED — 300-line cap is reasonable for ~5-10 line addition
round_1.EC3: STRENGTHENED — requires sync-local + test -f + make + non-behavioral label together, not any one of four alternatives
